question_text: Prove that the point on the parabola y² = 4ax, (a > 0), nearest to the focus is its vertex.

mark_split.label: Write the focal distance as a function of x₁
Minimise it and identify the point

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the focal distance as a function of x₁
steps.margin_note: First mark, for the focal distance formula and the reasoning that x₁ = 0 gives the minimum.
lines: The focal distance of any point P(x₁,y₁) on y²
Every point on this parabola has x₁ ≥ 0,
and a is a fixed positive number,
so SP = x₁ + a is smallest when x₁ = 0
steps.why: The focal distance formula SP = x₁ + a is an increasing function of x₁ alone, since a is fixed, so its smallest value over every point of the curve happens at the smallest possible x₁, which is 0.
common_mistakes: Trying to minimise SP using calculus (differentiating) instead of the simpler direct argument that x₁ + a grows as x₁ grows.
Forgetting to state that x₁ ≥ 0 is what makes x₁ = 0 the smallest allowed value, not just any small number.
steps.memory_tip: SP = x₁ + a only grows as x₁ grows, so its smallest value on the curve is at the smallest x₁, which is 0.

steps.label: Identify the nearest point
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for identifying the minimising point as the vertex itself.
steps.why: Substituting the minimising value x₁ = 0 back into the parabola's own equation pins down y₁ as well, and the resulting point (0,0) is exactly the vertex by definition.
common_mistakes: Stopping at x₁ = 0 without finding y₁ and naming the point as the vertex.
Assuming without checking that y₁ = 0 follows automatically, rather than substituting x₁ = 0 into y₁² = 4ax₁.
steps.memory_tip: Setting x₁ = 0 in y₁² = 4ax₁ always gives y₁ = 0 too — that point is the vertex by definition.

insider_note: This is a proof, not a calculation, so the final line has to name the vertex explicitly — simply stopping at x₁ = 0, y₁ = 0 without saying that this is the vertex misses the point of the question.
